items.title: Znanstvenici misle da se na rubu Sunčevog sustava skriva još jedan planet
items.summary: ASTRONOMI predlažu postojanje još jednog skrivenog planeta, 'Planet X2', na rubu Sunčevog sustava. Njegova gravitacija mogla bi objasniti neobične putanje udaljenih ledenih tijela.

items.title: Hidden for 100 million years: X-rays reveal an ancient flower from the age of dinosaurs
items.summary: In a new paper published in the American Journal of Botany, a team of scientists from the U.S. and UK reveal an incredible fossil from the mid-Cretaceous period (around 100 million years ago), opening up a new window into the early evolutionary history of modern-day plants.

items.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
items.summary: A next-generation geodetic instrument developed by NASA, part of a network that helps measure satellites’ orbits and the planet’s shape, has debuted in Svalbard, Norway.

items.summary: Fifty-two million years ago, the Pacific tectonic plate began to slide under the Philippine Sea plate, forming the Mariana Trench, the deepest known valley on the Earth's ocean floor. items.title: Reliance on technology is eroding trust in one another and ability to tell what is even real, expert warns
items.summary: The danger of generative AI is not some distant algorithmic failure; it is the slow erosion of our ability to tell what's real, to trust our institutions and to think for ourselves at all. These are the warnings of Mateusz Łabuz in his new book, The End of Reality.

items.summary: People with type 2 diabetes face a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease, according to a major new review of 40 studies. items.summary: How atoms are arranged in a material shapes many of its properties. items.title: Eksperimentalni češalj uspješno obnovio dlaku na miševima u samo mjesec dana
items.summary: EKSPERIMENTALNI elektronički češalj pokazao je iznimne rezultate u obnovi dlake na miševima s obrijanim leđima. Iako se radi o obećavajućem izumu, prerano je za zaključke o primjeni na ljudima.

items.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen emerges as a major nutrient source for global oceans
items.summary: A research team has quantified an important component of the global nitrogen cycle.

items.title: JWST finds a possible black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy in the early universe
items.summary: How the first massive black holes formed in the universe remains an open question in astronomy. Black holes weighing about a billion solar masses within the first billion years of the universe require extraordinary origin stories.

items.title: Mercury gets its first visitor in years as a pair of spacecraft loop into orbit
items.summary: A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet's mountain of mysteries.

items.title: COP31 fails to agree on climate deal in chaotic finale
items.summary: The COP31 climate talks headed for a historic defeat Sunday after the EU and other countries refused to endorse a pact that omitted fossil fuels as the summit lurched into record overtime in Turkey.

items.title: Hybrid nanocrystal surface reveals new way to tune interactions with infrared light
items.summary: A one-crystal-thick sheet made from two types of nanocrystals mixed in solution can amplify or suppress infrared light beyond the sum of its parts.

items.title: Parasite makes mice more attractive to blood-feeding bugs, which may aid its spread
items.summary: Some parasites, such as Trypanosoma rangeli and Trypanosoma cruzi, can be passed between mammals and blood-feeding insects called triatomine bugs. Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs.
